messages:
incident-bot: Pager: [sev2] Suspicious log-forwarder activity detected in staging. Large number of outbound PUTs to s3://external-logs-uploads. Potential exposure of Authorization headers (sample in logs). Trace: trace-9f3a. @oncall-night please ack.

Maria (sre): Acked. I'm investigating ingress. Can we pause the forwarder and block the destination bucket?

oncall-night (pager): Ack. Pausing now.

devops-bot: deploybot: pausing log-forwarder service staging/logshipper v3... success. -> staging/logshipper paused by oncall-night :white_check_mark: 

ryan (eng-infra): Confirmed forwarder config had destination s3://external-logs-uploads and `redact_headers: false`. This was an accidental override from a recent config push. Sample entry: ```PUT /upload 200
Headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXXXX
payload_id: abc123```

sre-rotations: Oof. Plan: 1) rotate any keys in logs (rotate API keys & AWS keys used by forwarder), 2) block bucket & remove public access, 3) run quick scan for leaked tokens in object payloads, 4) contact customers if tokens are sensitive. I'll start key rotation.

ryan (eng-infra): To rotate forwarder creds: `infractl secrets rotate --service logshipper-staging` — it will create new creds and update k8s secret. Kick it after rotation.

devops-bot: infractl secrets rotate job queued by sre-rotations. job-id: rotate-32321. Deploy will update staging logshipper once keys are ready.

support-lead: Support - can you confirm whether any customer PII included? Which customers might be affected?

Maria (sre): Running a grep across the stored objects for patterns (sk-, AKIA, Authorization). Quick scan shows ~42 objects containing 'Authorization: Bearer sk-'. Appears to be short-lived session tokens from internal test accounts, not production customer tokens. Still need legal review.

legal: Do not send external customer notices yet. Save copies of evidence and tag retention. Provide list of affected accounts and exact keys found.

sre-rotations: Rotating now. Steps: 1) disable forwarder (done), 2) rotate AWS creds (`infractl secrets rotate ...`), 3) revoke any API tokens found via `api-admin revoke --token <id>` (I'll hand off list).

oncall-night (pager): I'll monitor for any retries. Setting a 2hr watch. @maria please handoff remaining actions.

Maria (sre): Handoff: continue scan for tokens, collect list for legal/support, confirm object ACLs removed, and confirm rotation success. Add postmortem stub.

support-lead: Preparing customer impact matrix. So far no PII, mostly internal test tokens; still prepping comms if required.

legal: We'll review. If tokens are internal tests, likely internal notice only. If any customer tokens, we will escalate to privacy.

devops-bot: rotate-32321: rotation complete. New secrets injected into staging. logshipper will remain paused until manual check.

ryan (eng-infra): After rotation, don't redeploy until we scrub objects. Step to run: `s3cli ls s3://external-logs-uploads | xargs -n1 s3cli get-object | grep -E "Authorization:|AKIA|sk-"`

sre-rotations: Running scrub job now. Marking objects with sensitive markers and queueing deletion for confirmed artifacts.

Maria (sre): Summary for handoff -> Forwarder paused; creds rotated; ~42 objects flagged; legal and support notified; oncall-night monitoring for 2h; postmortem owner: maria. @oncall-night take it.

oncall-night (pager): Taking watch. If anything new shows up, I'll page SRE and infra. :eyes:
